messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: Help interpreting an error
parts:
Hi,

While working through converting my JAGS model to stan, I am coming across a strange error.  The model compiles fine.  Running everything from the command line.

Exception: Error in function stan::prob::uniform_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is nan:0, but must not be nan!
Diagnostic information:
Throw location unknown (consider using BOOST_THROW_EXCEPTION)
Dynamic exception type: boost::exception_detail::clone_impl<boost::exception_detail::error_info_injector<std::domain_error> >
std::exception::what: Error in function stan::prob::uniform_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is nan:0, but must not be nan!

However, I don't have a "uniform_log" call in my model.  The closest thing I have is:
     sigma_var_1 ~ uniform(0,00)

Any suggestions?

Thanks!

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help interpreting an error
parts:
It is just that the statement in Stan code such as 

a ~ distribution(...) 

gets translated to C++ code as 

lp__ += distribuion_log(...).  So in the case you have uniform distribution, it gets translated into uniform_log.  The manual is also using the form of "distribution_log" documenting all the distributions in Stan. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help interpreting an error
parts:
On Friday, November 30, 2012 1:54:29 PM UTC-5, Noah wrote:
I use the uniform as prior for variance for a few variables in the model:

example:

parameters{
real sigma_var_1;

The error in here: In Stan, you need to indicate the support of variables that have bounded support, such as non-negative variances. So, you need

real<lower=0> sigma_var_1;

The error you got was due to Stan proposing a value of sigma_var_1 that was negative, in which case the uniform(0,100) becomes undefined.

I would suggest reading Appendix C of the Stan manual and this FAQ

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/4gv3fNCqSNk/VonPUkdcZuUJ

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help interpreting an error
parts:
On Friday, November 30, 2012 2:06:44 PM UTC-5, Ben Goodrich wrote:
On Friday, November 30, 2012 1:54:29 PM UTC-5, Noah wrote:
I use the uniform as prior for variance for a few variables in the model:

example:

parameters{
real sigma_var_1;

The error in here: In Stan, you need to indicate the support of variables that have bounded support, such as non-negative variances. So, you need

real<lower=0> sigma_var_1;

Actually, you need

real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_var_1;

if you prior is uniform(0,100), in which case you don't need to explicitly specify the uniform prior, as mentioned in this 

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/4gv3fNCqSNk/VonPUkdcZuUJ

FAQ thread.

Ben

A
